questions.q: Why would a consultant query an interface table directly instead of only relying on the import process's report?
options: Because reports are never produced by Oracle Fusion
Because querying is required before every single screen click in Oracle Fusion
Because a direct query shows the raw, current state of the staged data with no summarizing or interpretation
Because interface tables cannot be queried at all
questions.explain: Interface tables are ordinary database tables. A direct query gives you the unfiltered, current state of what's staged, which a summarized report doesn't always fully capture.

questions.q: What is the value of querying an interface table BEFORE running the real import process?
options: It prevents the import process from ever being needed
It has no value since the import process checks everything anyway
It automatically fixes any data problems found
It lets you sanity-check row counts and values — catching a loading problem early, before business-rule validation even runs
questions.explain: A quick pre-import query is a cheap way to catch an obviously wrong row count or malformed value before spending time running the actual import process.

questions.q: After an import process runs, what typically remains in the interface table?
options: Every row, regardless of success or failure, unchanged
Rows that were rejected — successful rows typically leave the table or are marked processed
Nothing at all, regardless of outcome
Only rows that were never loaded in the first place
questions.explain: Successfully imported rows generally leave the interface table (or are marked as processed), while rejected rows tend to remain, often alongside a related rejections table.

questions.q: What's the benefit of querying an interface table together with a related rejections table?
options: It shows the original staged data alongside the specific reason each row was rejected, without depending entirely on the formatted report
It permanently deletes all rejected rows
It automatically re-runs the import process
There is no benefit — rejections tables don't exist
questions.explain: Joining the interface table with a rejections table on a shared row identifier gives the full picture: the data as entered, plus the exact reason it failed.

questions.q: Why do the column names you recognize from an FBDI template matter when writing a query against an interface table?
options: They don't — template columns and table columns are unrelated
Because templates use entirely different naming conventions than any database table
Because a template's column headers are literal interface-table column names, so the same names appear in both places
Because queries never reference column names
questions.explain: As covered in Chapter 2, a template's column headers are the literal names of the interface table's columns, so reading a template and querying its table use the same vocabulary.
